# Best travel chargers with multiple USB-C ports

**Top pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port.** Several reviewers name it best overall for mixed travel kits. It has three USB-C ports and one USB-A. Sources disagree on this: one says four USB-C, but most say 3 USB-C + 1 USB-A, so check the listing before buying.
- **Power:** Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With a laptop and a second device, it splits to about 65W and 30W. With all four ports in use, it's about 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the remaining ports.
- **Downsides:** It's the heaviest of the group at 8.3 oz, and no cable is included.
- **Where to buy:** The "Check price" buttons are in the reviews. I don't have a direct product URL.
  - [TechWise: best GaN travel chargers](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026)
  - [TechWise: best chargers for multiple devices](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)
  - [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger)

**Other options**

- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W** is best if a power-hungry laptop is your priority. It has two USB-C ports and one USB-A, and the 120W is shared once several devices connect. [Review and buy link](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)
- **Anker Prime 67W (3-port)** is the smallest and lightest at 4.78 oz. It has two USB-C ports, either of which can deliver the full 67W alone, and PPS support for Samsung and Pixel phones. It's the right size for one laptop plus a phone. [Review and buy link](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W** has two USB-C ports and one USB-A, and it's about $49.99 for a 2-pack at Baseus's US store (price verified 2026-10-21). With two or three devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is fine for a MacBook Air but not a full-speed 65W laptop. [Buy at Baseus](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (affiliate link)
- **Baseus EnerCore CG11** is best if you're going abroad and don't want a separate plug adapter. It has swappable plugs and a built-in cable, but only one USB-C port plus two USB-A. [Android Central guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel)

**Things to know**
- The wattage on the box is the total. Plug in a laptop first and use the remaining ports for phones and earbuds.
- All of these have US prongs. Outside the US you need a plug adapter, not a voltage converter, since they accept 100-240V.
- For 100W, use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable. A plain USB-C cable is only rated for 60W.
- These are review-site picks based on published specs, not my own testing. Prices change, so confirm them on the listing.

If you tell me what you're charging (laptop model, phone, tablet) and where you're traveling, I can narrow it to one.
